If you are relatively healthy and would like to optimize your expenses as a young entrepreneur, you can opt for a cost-effective private insurance tariff with ottonova. Later, when you have successfully built up your business, you can switch to a tariff focused on more extensive care. - **More comprehensive benefits:** If you want to always be fully covered, you can choose a tariff with the most extensive benefits. For example, with ottonova you can get a private room at the hospital or complete coverage of your new dentures. Some benefits, such as age-independent preventive examinations and health cover abroad are included in all tariffs, in contrast to the public health insurance. In addition, you can set up a daily sickness allowance as a compensation for your lost earnings during long-term illness. - **Faster to the doctor:** Private patients often get specialist appointments faster. What many insurers know from experience is also confirmed by social field studies: It takes around 25 days for a publicly insured person to get a specialist appointment, while privately insured patients wait only 12 days on average. - **More doctors to choose from:** Some medical practices only take privately insured patients and self-payers. As a member of private health insurance, you can also be treated there without any problems and be reimbursed. This can be important if you are looking for a doctor with a specific approach. ### Why does private health insurance for the self-employed, freelancers & new business founders make sense? Your private health insurance premium is based on your entry age and state of health at the time of conclusion of the contract, not on your income. Private health insurance is as flexible as you are: you get to choose the insurance cover that suits you best. Your health is reliably protected through fast access to specialists and modern treatment methods. As an entrepreneur, with private health insurance you can collect provisions for the future with aging reserves and options to further reduce premiums in old age. Your digital lifestyle is covered everywhere – depending on the tariff there is worldwide protection and care for your health. ### How do founders & freelancers find the right private health insurance? The costs and benefits of individual insurance companies can vary greatly. An in-depth comparison is worthwhile to find the best offer! Which factors you should check: 1. **Coverage:** Think about which benefits matter the most to you. Maybe a shared room in a hospital is enough for you, but you want to cover your teeth with 100 % reimbursement for dental replacements? Set priorities and think about what they are worth to you. 2. **Deductible:** Would you rather have less co-pay or more? A high deductible often goes with favorable rates. Calculate whether you are likely to spend below your annual deductible cap and whether it really brings a saving. At ottonova, there is only a percentage deductible: You pay 10 or 25 percent of your medical bills yourself, until you reach a limit of 500 or 1,250 euros per year. This way, you benefit from the reimbursements right from the start and you won't be tempted to skip annual preventive examinations to save money. 3. **Costs:** It is important to consider not only the current costs of your private health insurance, but also the contribution development over time. After all, you want your costs to still be in line when you go into well-earned retirement. At ottonova, we calculate our premiums using a particularly future-proof actuarial interest rate. ### How to calculate the cost of health insurance for a self-employed person? Self-employed people and freelancers must pay the entire health insurance contribution, regardless of whether they are publicly or privately insured, since they do not have an employer who pays an employer subsidy for health insurance. If you join private health insurance as a business founder or a self-employed person, your contribution depends on your age, your pre-existing conditions and your health condition, as well as your preferred tariff. With ottonova, for example, the monthly contribution is around 552 to 654 euros for a person at the age of 32. - Adjustable contribution independent of income - Family members co-insured at their own premiums - Change to public health insurance only with employment **Your contribution in private health insurance depends on:** - entry age - health history at the time of conclusion of the contract - coverage You can adjust your contribution with a deductible or a daily sickness allowance. As a young entrepreneur or tradesman with a good income, you often pay less than in the public health insurance. **Contribution for public health insurance** - Contribution depends on income - Family members insured free of charge - Change to private health insurance possible at any time Your contribution for self-employed persons in public health insurance depends on this: - Reduced contribution rate: 14.00% (without sick pay), general contribution rate: 14.60% (with sick pay) - Additional contribution for individual health insurances: on average 2.90% (varies depending on the health insurance company) - Nursing care insurance: 4.2% (without children), 3.6% (with children) **Important**: The calculation basis for your public health insurance rate is your income tax assessment or a profit estimate if you are just starting out. If you earn more than expected, you will have to pay extra. The only possibility to influence your public health insurance premium is the “additional contribution” which is individual for each public health insurance fund. ### Who is considered self-employed? Self-employed are those who work freely and without a dependent employment relationship. A private health insurance for entrepreneurs or tradespeople is part of being independent too. The forms of self-employment are further differentiated: Freelancer or tradesperson? It depends: **Tradesmen** If you do not carry out a "catalog profession”, you are a trader and pay trade tax. In your tax return, you can deduct your private health insurance for the self-employed. **Freelancer** Freelancer is a term for different professions. It can mean that you work for a company without a fixed employment contract or that you have a freelance profession like writing, artistic or scientific work, or teaching. §18 of the Income Tax Act provides a catalog of activities: Among others, engineers, tax advisors, consultants, physicians, or lawyers are freelancers and do not pay trade tax. **Exception: artists and publicists** If you are a freelancer working in the arts or journalism, you are still required to have statutory health insurance. This means that you remain subject to compulsory insurance even if your annual income exceeds the income threshold. In order to switch to private health insurance, you must apply for exemption from compulsory insurance within the first three months of your freelance activity. If you want to switch to private health insurance after that, you must prove that you have earned more than three times the annual income limit (€36,355) in the last three years (e.g., €100,000 + €50,000 + €80,000). The Artists' Social Insurance Fund (Künstlersozialkasse) provides a subsidy for pension insurance and health insurance, including private health insurance, for freelance artistic or journalistic work. ### 3 reasons why self-employed people insured at ottonova are in the best hands - **Full control** With private health insurance, you can choose between different tariffs and components such as daily sickness allowance or deductible options, and adapt your monthly cost according to your needs. So, you are more flexible and get more extensive benefits. With the daily sickness allowance you also insure yourself against loss of earnings in the event of illness. ### How do self-employed switch to private health insurance? Many self-employed opt for private health insurance to benefit from the extensive benefits of private health insurance. However, choosing the right policy needs to be well thought out! Take your time to compare the different tariffs. If you want to change to private health insurance, you must submit an application. It is best to take care of this before you become self-employed to ensure seamless insurance coverage. **Observe notice periods:** If you are voluntarily insured under the statutory health insurance scheme, the notice period for statutory health insurance is two months. So if you give notice on October 1, for example, you can take out private health insurance for the month after next, i.e. January 1. For self-employed persons who were previously compulsorily insured under the statutory health insurance system, however, the notice period is irrelevant, as you can leave the statutory health insurance system at the start of your self-employment, even retroactively. ### Public or private health insurance for the self-employed? 5 tips for your decision. **1\. Under the private health insurance system, every family member needs their own individual policy, and the cost (premium) is calculated based on each person's health and age when they enroll. Because of this, children's premiums are typically quite affordable. To insure your children in private health insurance can have a lot of advantages. If you are young, self-employed and are likely to pay the maximum premium for public health insurance, if you value high-quality benefits for your health and if you want to make yourself independent of demographic change and make individual provisions for later. ### What happens if I am sick for a long period of time as a self-employed person? If at some point you decide to change your self-employment back to employment, your income will count: If you are above the annual income threshold, you can remain in the private health insurance. If your salary is below this limit, you are subject to compulsory insurance and can return to the public health insurance, provided you are not yet 55 years old. But as an self-employed person you can of course stay with us. With a qualifying period, you secure your right to return to us without a new health check. We will also continue to pay interest on your aging provisions. If you wish, we can then extend your public health insurance coverage with sensible top-up dental- and hospital care supplementary insurance tariffs. ### What does health insurance for freelancers cost? **Public health insurance:** - Your premium depends on your (estimated) income, there are minimum and maximum limits. - The general cost for health insurance is 14.6% of your gross income per month. You also need to may your nursing care insurance (general rate is 4% of gross income). - Your premium can also be influenced by the “additional contribution”  (Zusatzbeitrag) which is individual for each public health insurance fund (average around 1,2% of your gross income). - If you do not have any children, oyu pay an additional premium for childless people (around 0,6% of your gross income). There may be additional payments at the end of the year. **Private health insurance:** - Your premium depends on your state of health and age at the moment that you start the contract and your desired benefits. - As the contract goes on, your age and health have no further effect on the development of your premium, it is held stable from any individual influences. - Your monthly premium can be tailored with components such as deductibles. There are no additional payments at the end of the year. ### What role does the deductible play for me as a self-employed person? A higher deductible leads to a lower monthly premium. This reduces your monthly fixed costs - since you don't receive an employer's contribution like an employee does. With ottonova, all dental care as well as the preventive yearly health check-up are deductible free, always. For other claims, you can choose a 50% deductible in the tariff Premium Economy or 25% deductible in Business and First Class. That means, that you will be getting either 50% or 75% of the claim back right away from the first claim. Do not worry, as you will not have to co-pay your 50% or 25% for non-dental care indefinitely. Your deductible has a yearly cap, which limits your maximum out-of-pocket spending per year. If your co-paid 50% reach 1000€ or 25% reach 1250€ in a year, that is the maximum and you will not have any deductible at all till the rest of the year. Want an **Example?** If you choose Premium Economy with 50% deductible and then you go for a dental filling that costs 100€, you will get the 100€ reimbursed back to you right away. Same for the health check with your primary doctor (Hausarzt). If you then go for a dermatology appointment which costs 100€ and send the claim, you will get 50€ reimbursed from us and when you pay the doctor the full sum, you will spend 50% (50€ in this case) out-of-pocket. Then out of your maximum 1000€per year, 950€ will remain. The nice part is that if you have a really large cost, e.g. 5000€ for something non-dental, then even though 50% of 5000€ would be 2500€, anyway your out-of-pocket spending is capped at 1000€. In a normal year, most people do not even reach the cap and have a few hundreds out-of-pocket at most. ### What benefits do I get as a self-employed person or self-employed person when I work abroad? If you wish, we can then extend your public health insurance coverage with sensible top-up dental- and hospital care supplementary insurance tariffs. **These supplementary top-up insurances then make sense:** [Supplementary hospital insurance](https://ottonova.de/en/v/hospitalization-insurance) [Supplementary dental insurance](https://www.ottonova.de/en/v/hospitalization-insurance) ### How does the ottonova no-claim bonus work for self-employed? Every individual covered under the **First Class Pro+ and Business Class Pro** tariffs for self-employed individuals is eligible for a guaranteed no-claim bonus. To qualify for the no-claim bonus, **no claims must have been filed in the previous calendar year**. However, we understand the importance of maintaining good health, so essential preventive check-ups are still encouraged. Consequently, you can still benefit from the following services while also receiving the no-claim bonus: - Professional dental cleanings according to GoÄ - Benefits for preventive check-ups according to statutory programs - Vaccinations (excluding travel vaccinations) The premium refund will be disbursed in the **latter half of the subsequent year** if insurance coverage have been maintained without interruption throughout the entire calendar year. The amount of the guaranteed no-claim bonus is determined by taking the total premiums paid (excluding statutory surcharges) for the preceding calendar year and dividing it by 12. If you have any inquiries regarding whether an invoice impacts the no-claim bonus, the ottonova concierge is available to assist you. [Skip to content](https://germanpedia.com/health-insurance-for-self-employed-and-freelancers-germany/#content) [Home](https://germanpedia.com/) » [Insurance](https://germanpedia.com/insurance/) » [Health Insurance in Germany](https://germanpedia.com/insurance/health/) » Health Insurance For Self-Employed And Freelancers # Health Insurance for Self-Employed and Freelancers in Germany \[2026 English Guide\] Author: [GermanPedia Staff](https://germanpedia.com/author/contact/ "GermanPedia Staff") Last Updated: November 28, 2025 \| Views: 1,222 ## Key takeaways - Self-employed and freelancers must have health insurance in Germany ( [§ 5 SGB V](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_5/__5.html)). - You can choose between private and [public health insurance](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/gesetzliche-krankenversicherung/). - You can deduct the contributions to the basic health and [long-term care insurance](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/pflegeversicherung/) in full. - Freelancers pursuing artistic or journalistic activity must get public health insurance via the [Artist’s social insurance fund (Künstlersozialkasse (KSK))](https://germanpedia.com/artists-social-insurance-fund/). ## This is how you do it - Understand the [differences between public and private health insurance](https://germanpedia.com/public-or-private-health-insurance-germany/) in Germany. Pay special attention to contributions, family coverage, switching rules, and long-term costs before you decide. - Play with our “ [Health Insurance Finder](https://germanpedia.com/health-insurance-finder-germany/)” tool to learn which health insurance (Public or Private) makes sense and when. - We recommend getting [private health insurance](https://germanpedia.com/private-health-insurance-germany/) via an insurance broker. They are experts and can help you find the best plan for your needs. You can book a call with an expert we recommend [here](https://germanpedia.com/contact-health-insurance-broker-germany/). - In our [comparison and test](https://germanpedia.com/best-private-health-insurance-comparison-germany/), we found Haellesche, Allianz, and Signal Iduna's [private health insurance](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/pkv/) plans to be the best. ## Table of contents ## Health insurance for self-employed and freelancers in Germany Health insurance is mandatory in Germany. Self-employed and freelancers can choose between - public health insurance - private health insurance - artist’s social insurance ### Artist’s Social Insurance Freelancers pursuing artistic or journalistic activity can get public health insurance via [artists’ social insurance (Künstlersozialversicherung in German)](https://germanpedia.com/artists-social-insurance-fund/) ( [KSVG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ksvg/)). You can also opt for private health insurance. You must apply for the exemption from compulsory public health insurance within 3 months of starting your career as a freelancer. The exemption from compulsory [public health insurance](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/gesetzliche-krankenversicherung/) automatically ends after 6 years (per Social Insurance Act [§ 6 KSVG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ksvg/__6.html)). You must [switch from private to public health insurance](https://germanpedia.com/private-to-public-health-insurance/) once the exemption ends. The only way to stay in private health insurance is if you earn more than the [compulsory insurance limit](https://germanpedia.com/contribution-assessment-ceiling-germany/) (i.e., 77,400€ (as of 2026)) in the previous three years. > **NOTE:** If you exempt yourself from the statutory health insurance via KSK, you can never return to public health insurance via KSK. You can return to public health insurance (without the KSK support) in certain situations only. ### Private health insurance Full-time self-employed individuals can get private health insurance without any restrictions. Moreover, there is no [minimum income threshold](https://germanpedia.com/contribution-assessment-ceiling-germany/) for self-employed people ( [§ 6 SGB V](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_5/__6.html)) to join [private insurance](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/pkv/). On the other hand, employees must earn more than the [income threshold](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/jahresarbeitsentgeltgrenze-jaeg/) (Jahresarbeitsentgeltgrenze, JAEG) (i.e., 77,400€ (as of 2026)) to be eligible to apply for private health insurance. If you are part-time self-employed, your main job determines whether you can get private health insurance. ### Public health insurance If you are self-employed, you can become a voluntary member of a statutory health insurance fund. The rules for voluntary membership are set out in [§ 9 SGB V](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_5/__9.html). Whether you are eligible for [public health insurance](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/gesetzliche-krankenversicherung/) depends on your - previous insurance history (you were previously insured in the public or private system), - your nationality (EU or non-EU), and - type of visa (long-term or short-term visa) **Publicly insured before becoming self-employed** In this case, you must meet the following criteria to continue in the public system. You must have been compulsorily insured for - at least 12 uninterrupted months before becoming self-employed, **or** - 24 months within the last five years. If you meet the eligibility criteria, you must apply for **voluntary** statutory insurance within three months after the end of **compulsory** public insurance. **Privately insured before becoming self-employed** In this case, it’s tough to get public health insurance, and you must continue with your private health insurance. There are particular situations in which you can get public health insurance. For example, you don’t earn from your self-employment and can be insured under your spouse’s public health insurance for free. We suggest [consulting an insurance broker](https://germanpedia.com/contact-health-insurance-broker-germany/) to discuss your case in detail. ## What are the consequences of not taking health insurance in Germany? Here are the consequences for not getting health insurance on time. - Health insurers may demand retroactive contributions ( [Beitragsnachforderungen](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/beitragsnachforderungen/)). - You may face legal consequences (for example, insurance fraud under [§ 266a StGB](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/stgb/__266a.html)). Employers ensure that their employees have valid health insurance in Germany. However, freelancers and self-employed people must take care of their health insurance themselves. ## What health insurance is better for the self-employed in Germany – public or private? Let’s understand the differences between private and [public health insurance](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/gesetzliche-krankenversicherung/) to see which is right for the self-employed in Germany. | Statutory health insurance for self-employed | Private health insurance for self-employed | | --- | --- | | **Factors on which health insurance cost depends.** | | | Public health insurance costs depend on your income, number of children, and whether you’ll opt for [sick pay](https://germanpedia.com/sick-leave-germany/).
Your insurance premium decreases and increases with the decrease and increase of your income. | [Private health insurance costs](https://germanpedia.com/health-insurance-costs-germany/) depend on your age, health, occupation, and services you opt for.
It doesn’t depend on your income. Thus, your insurance premium will remain the same even if your income decreases. | | **How much is the insurance premium?** | | | Public health insurance costs comprise two things.
– **Basic amount: 14%** of your gross monthly income (no [sick pay](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/krankengeld/)). **14.6%** of your gross monthly income (with sick pay)( [§ 241 SGB V](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_5/__241.html)) _._
– **[Additional contribution](https://germanpedia.com/public-health-insurance-additional-contribution-germany/)**( [Zusatzbeitrag](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/zusatzbeitrag/)): **2.9% (as of 2026)** of your gross monthly income
Public insurance providers decide the Zusatzbeitrag. Zusatzbeitrag of some insurers like [TK](https://germanpedia.com/register-with-tk/) is 2.45% (lower than 2.9% (as of 2026)). And some insurers’ Zusatzbeitrag is higher than 2.9% (as of 2026). | Based on our research, [good private health insurance plans cost](https://germanpedia.com/health-insurance-costs-germany/) between
– **466 € and 683 € per month to self-employed**
– **301 € and 355 € per month to employees**(The cost is after deducting the employer’s contributions are already deducted)
– **288 € and 400 € per month to civil servants** | | **Nursing care insurance cost** | | | 3.6% of your gross monthly salary (as of 2026) for self-employed people with one child and 4.2% of your gross monthly salary (as of 2026) with no children ( [§ 55 SGB XI](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_11/__55.html)) | Included in the above [private insurance](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/pkv/) costs. | | **Minimum monthly premium** | | | If you haven’t started earning from your business yet, you must still pay a minimum health insurance premium. As of 2026, the minimum monthly premium is between **278 € and 286 €.**
**How is the minimum premium calculated?**
Public insurers consider the minimum income for calculating the insurance premium: 1,318.33€ (as of 2026)
**Case 1: No child**
– Basic amount: 192.47 € (14.6% of 1318.33)
– Additional contribution: 38.23 € (2.9% of 1318.33)
– Nursing care: 55.36 € (4.2% of 1318.33)
– Minimum monthly premium: 286.06 € (192.47 + 32.95 + 55.36)
**Case 2: One child**
– Basic amount: 192.47 € (14.6% of 1318.33)
– [Additional contribution](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/zusatzbeitrag/): 38.23 € (2.9% of 1318.33)
– Nursing care: 47.45 € (3.6% of 1318.33)
– Minimum monthly premium: 278.15 € (192.47 + 32.95 + 55.36) | It depends on age, health, occupation, and the services you opt for. | | **Maximum monthly premium** | | | There is a maximum [limit on how much gross income](https://germanpedia.com/contribution-assessment-ceiling-germany/) public insurers can consider when calculating the premium. It is 5812.5€ per month (as of 2026).
Thus, the maximum monthly premium in [public health insurance](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/gesetzliche-krankenversicherung/) is **1261€ per month (as of 2026)**. | It depends on age, health, occupation, and the services you opt for. There is no maximum limit. | | **Family health insurance** | | | Your spouse (if they don’t have any income) and children are covered for free under your public health insurance ( [§ 10 SGB V](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_5/__10.html)). | You must take a separate health insurance policy for your spouse and each child. | | **What happens if I am unemployed or have no income?** | | | If you receive “Unemployment Benefit I” from the job center, you remain insured with your public health insurance provider. Your insurer will get the monthly contribution directly from the job center.
If you don’t get “Unemployment Benefit I,” you can voluntarily insure under statutory health insurance. In this case, you must pay the minimum insurance premium. | – If you receive “Unemployment Benefits I,” you’ll automatically be covered by statutory health insurance, even if you previously had private insurance.
– You cannot switch to [statutory health insurance](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/gesetzliche-krankenversicherung/) if you are 55 and over. It doesn’t matter if you receive “Unemployment Benefit I.” 
– You can stay with your [private health insurer after being unemployed](https://germanpedia.com/health-insurance-for-unemployed-germany/) if you have had private insurance for five years before becoming unemployed. The job center pays a subsidy for your health insurance contributions.
– Privately insured people who receive “Unemployment benefit II” remain in private health insurance. You get a subsidy from the job center.
**NOTE**: You get the unemployment benefit only if you continue contributing to the unemployment insurance. | | **Sickness benefits** | | | Your basic amount increases from 14% to 14.6% if you opt for sickness benefits. Sickness benefits are paid by the public health insurance company when you are sick for the long term. 
You get [sick pay](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/krankengeld/) from the 43rd day of your illness. You can take an optional tariff if you want to start getting paid earlier ( [§ 47 SGB V](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_5/__47.html)).
You can compare different daily sickness benefits insurance on the comparison portal [Check24](https://a.partner-versicherung.de/click.php?partner_id=136006&ad_id=15&deep=krankenzusatzversicherung)\*. | While choosing private health insurance, you can decide on the daily sickness allowance and when to start getting it. | | **Changing health insurance plan with the same provider** | | | Statutory health insurance providers have standard coverage and don’t offer multiple plans. 
Of course, you can take supplementary [private health insurance](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/pkv/) on top. | You can [switch to a better health insurance plan](https://germanpedia.com/switch-private-health-insurance-plan-germany/) offered by your insurer. However, the insurer may demand a complete health check.
Depending on the health check results and services in the new tariff, your health insurance premium might be higher than the older tariff. | | **Changing health insurance provider** | | | You can change your public health insurance provider anytime. You can use our [public health insurance cost calculator](https://germanpedia.com/public-health-insurance-cost-calculator/) to check how much you save by switching the insurer. | Changing private health insurance providers in Germany is expensive. 
– You lose a large part of your saved [retirement provisions](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/private-health-insurance-retirement-provisions/).
– A new [health insurer](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/krankenkasse/) will demand a complete health check. Hence, it might lead to higher insurance costs.
– You usually pay a higher premium to the new insurer as you age. | | **Switching between private and public health insurance in Germany** | | | You can switch from public to private health insurance anytime. | [Returning to the public health insurance system](https://germanpedia.com/private-to-public-health-insurance/) is tough. It’s almost impossible for people 55 and older to make the switch.
If you cannot return to the public system, you can switch to a “Basistarif” of your private insurer. Every private health insurance company must offer “Basistarif”. Its benefits are comparable to those of [public insurance](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/gesetzliche-krankenversicherung/). The Basistarif is regulated under [§ 12 VAG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/vag_2016/__12.html) and [§ 193 VVG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/vvg_2008/__193.html). | ## Conclusion: The right health insurance for the self-employed in Germany ### Artist’s health insurance If you qualify for an artist’s health insurance, get it. The reason is that KSK contributes half of the health insurance premium, and you pay the other half ( [§ 10 KSVG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/ksvg/__10.html)). You can pick any public health insurance company of your choice. **[Artist’s health insurance ->](https://germanpedia.com/artists-social-insurance-fund/)** ### Public health insurance Public health insurance is the safest choice. If you are unsure about which health insurance to pick, just go with public insurance. Here is why. - Premium depends on your income. - You can insure your non-earning family members for free. In general, if you have just started your business and don’t have a stable income, public health insurance is the right choice. **[Best public health insurance ->](https://germanpedia.com/best-public-health-insurance-germany/)** ### Private health insurance Private health insurance (PKV) is usually a good choice for high-income and healthy self‑employed people. If you earn more than the income threshold, you save between 290€ and 500€ per month. But it’s the gross savings. You must also deduct income tax on this amount. Assuming you earn more than 77,400€ (as of 2026), your [personal income tax rate will be 42%](https://germanpedia.com/tax-classes-germany). Thus, your net savings will be between 168€ and 290€ per month. Good [private health insurance](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/pkv/) plans also offer better coverage than [public insurance](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/gesetzliche-krankenversicherung/). You can use our “ [Health Insurance Finder](https://germanpedia.com/health-insurance-finder-germany/)” tool to help you choose between private and public insurance based on your life situation. If you are unsure, get personalised advice from an [independent insurance broker](https://germanpedia.com/contact-health-insurance-broker-germany/) or a Verbraucherzentrale (consumer advice centre). **[Best private health insurance plans ->](https://germanpedia.com/best-private-health-insurance-comparison-germany/)** ## **Health insurance for part-time self-employed** Suppose you are full-time employed and doing your business part-time. In this case, your main job decides which health insurance you can get. You can have private health insurance if your income from the job is more than the income threshold (i.e., 77,400€ (as of 2026)). Otherwise, you are compulsorily insured under public health insurance. Health insurance companies consider your self-employment part-time in the following situations. - You work less than 20 hours per week on your business. - Your primary source of income is from your job. In other words, the income from your business does not serve to ensure your main livelihood. - You don’t employ any employee subject to social security contributions. **[How to hire your first employee in Germany ->](https://germanpedia.com/hiring-in-germany/)** ## How do you get health insurance as a self-employed or freelancer in Germany? ### Artist’s social insurance (KSK) for self-employed in Germany You can apply for the artists’ social insurance [online on KSK’s website](https://www.kuenstlersozialkasse.de/kuenstler-und-publizisten/anmeldung.html). KSK will verify if you meet the requirements. You are free to choose any public health insurer. ### Public health insurance for self-employed persons and freelancers in Germany You have two ways to get a statutory health insurance policy in Germany: - Via an [insurance broker](https://germanpedia.com/contact-health-insurance-broker-germany/) or agent - Directly from the public health insurance company. If you don’t speak German, you can use our service to [register with TK online](https://germanpedia.com/register-with-tk/) in English. You can also apply directly on the public insurer’s website. Many health insurance providers in Germany have websites in German and English. ### Private health insurance for freelancers in Germany Like [public health insurance](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/gesetzliche-krankenversicherung/), you can get a private insurance policy via - an [insurance broker](https://germanpedia.com/contact-health-insurance-broker-germany/), - comparison portals ( [Tarifcheck](https://germanpedia.com/check24-private-health-insurance)\*), and - directly from the insurance company. However, we recommend consulting an insurance broker or a fee-based adviser for personalized advice before taking private health insurance in Germany. ## Book a free call with a health insurance expert ![](https://fefffe12.delivery.rocketcdn.me/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/book-a-call-broker-1024x1024.webp) - **German health insurance is a complicated product.** There are several factors that must be considered before deciding which health insurance is best for you. An expert can guide you and help you pick the best option for you. - **An Insurance broker is liable for their advice.** This means if the policy they recommended doesn’t offer the coverage you requested, they are liable to pay the damages incurred in the future. [Book a call](https://germanpedia.com/contact-health-insurance-broker-germany/) ## Statutory health insurance coverage in Germany Public health insurance is regulated by the Fifth Book of the Social Code (SGB V). Insured persons are entitled to necessary medical treatment as set out in the law ( [§ 27 SGB V](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_5/__27.html)). The law states that the publicly insured person is entitled to adequate, needs-based medical treatment corresponding to the generally recognized state of medical science. This includes - medical treatment, - [dental treatment](https://germanpedia.com/dental-treatment-cost-germany/), - psychotherapeutic treatment, - the supply of medicines, bandages, remedies, aids, - home nursing care, - hospital treatment, - medical rehabilitation services, and other services. The law specifies that medical services must be sufficient, appropriate, and economical. Services must not exceed what is necessary ( [§ 12 SGB V](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/sgb_5/__12.html)). Every public health insurance provider must offer services regulated by law. Thus, there is little difference in the services that different public health insurance providers offer. > **NOTE**: The German public healthcare system is under a lot of pressure due to demographic change and increased medical costs. Thus, the [public health insurance premium will rise drastically in the near future](https://germanpedia.com/private-health-insurance-cost-development/). ## Private health insurance coverage in Germany Private health insurance companies offer many plans, from basic to comprehensive coverage. Thus, it is critical to [check and compare the services](https://germanpedia.com/private-health-insurance-benefits-in-germany/) before signing the health insurance contract. > **NOTE**: [Private health insurance](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/pkv/) companies are better prepared for the future. This is because they save at least 10% of your monthly premium as a retirement provision ( [§ 149 VAG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/vag_2016/__149.html)). How private health insurance companies can use the reserves is also defined in law ( [§ 150 VAG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/vag_2016/__150.html)). Here are some essential services a good private health insurance should cover. - Doctors’ fees - Freedom to select the doctor - [Low deductible](https://germanpedia.com/health-insurance-deductibles-germany/) - Check if there are any reimbursement limits. - Your private health insurance provider should cover the cost of both generic and non-generic medicines. - What life support and physical aids does your private insurance cover? - Dental benefits - Ensure that the psychotherapy coverage in your [private health insurance](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/pkv/) matches that of your public insurance. - What type of therapies does your health insurance plan cover? [**Minimum services your private health insurance must cover ->**](https://germanpedia.com/private-health-insurance-benefits-in-germany/) You can download our checklist to ensure your policy covers the minimum recommended services. ## Private health insurance services checklist ![private health insurance benefits checklist](https://fefffe12.delivery.rocketcdn.me/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Private-health-insurance-benefits-checklist-1024x1024.webp) - A comprehensive list of services good private insurance should cover. - Use it during your consultation with an insurance broker or a fee-based advisor. - Use it while searching for a private health insurance policy. [Free Download](https://germanpedia.gumroad.com/l/tekvi) ## FAQs **1\. Can you switch from Private to [Public Health Insurance](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/gesetzliche-krankenversicherung/) in Germany?** Switching from private to public health insurance is difficult. And it gets tougher as you grow old. There are a few ways to return to the public healthcare system. For example, – You get a job and your salary goes below the [income threshold](https://germanpedia.com/contribution-assessment-ceiling-germany/). – You shut down your business and receive “unemployment benefit I.” – You shut down your business (unemployed) and want to be insured under your spouse’s public health insurance. [**How to return from private to statutory health insurance? ->**](https://germanpedia.com/private-to-public-health-insurance) **2\. Can freelancers and self-employed deduct health insurance premiums from taxes?** Contributions for health insurance that cover the basic, statutory-equivalent insurance (Basisabsicherung) are fully [deductible](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/deductible/) ( [§ 10 EStG](https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/estg/__10.html)). Additional benefits (e.g., high daily sickness allowance, private room, etc.) are deductible up to the maximum limit set by the tax office. The maximum limit is €2,800 per year (as of 2026) for self-employed and €1,900 per year (as of 2026) for employees, civil servants, and pensioners. **[How to deduct health insurance premiums from taxes? ->](https://germanpedia.com/tax-deductible-health-insurance-costs-germany/)** **3\. I am self-employed part-time. How does it affect my health insurance?** If you are **employed full-time and self-employed part-time**, your health insurance via employment will continue. However, you must inform the health insurance company about your part-time self-employment. The health insurer will determine whether your self-employed work is part-time. If the health insurer determines it’s not part-time, your compulsory public health insurance via employment will end. You must take out voluntary public health insurance or private insurance. In this case, your employer will stop contributing to your health insurance premiums. Similarly, if you are **unemployed and self-employed part-time**, you can continue to be covered under your spouse’s [public health insurance](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/gesetzliche-krankenversicherung/). But [free family insurance](https://germanpedia.com/family-insurance-germany/) ends in the following cases. – Your earnings exceed the family-insurance threshold. – Your public [health insurer](https://germanpedia.com/glossary/krankenkasse/) considers your self-employment not marginal. **4\. What happens if you cannot afford health insurance premiums as a self-employed?** **Publicly insured individuals have the following options.** – Insure yourself in family insurance via your spouse. – Apply for state support. **Privately insured self-employed and freelancers who cannot pay insurance premiums** anymore fall into the emergency tariff. In an emergency tariff, you get the minimum health services. But as soon as you can afford the health insurance premiums, you must return to your original tariff. You should consider [reducing your private health insurance premium](https://germanpedia.com/reduce-private-health-insurance-costs-germany/) if you cannot afford it. The easiest way to do so is by [switching to a cheaper tariff](https://germanpedia.com/switch-private-health-insurance-plan-germany/) offered by your insurance provider. [**Health insurance when you are unemployed ->**](https://germanpedia.com/health-insurance-for-unemployed-germany/) **5\. What is the Künstlersozialkasse? Why should I take it?** The Artists’ Social Fund ( [Künstlersozialkasse (KSK)](https://www.kuenstlersozialkasse.de/)) is an organization that checks your eligibility to join the fund. It also collects health insurance premiums and forwards them to the relevant public health insurance providers. You can get health insurance via the artists’ social insurance fund if you – do artistic or journalistic activity commercially, – you do not employ more than one employee (except for trainees and mini-jobbers), – you earn at least 3,901 euros per year (more than 325 euros per month) from your artistic work. The benefit of getting health insurance via the artist’s fund is that you only pay half of the health insurance premiums. Read our [guide on the artists’ social insurance fund](https://germanpedia.com/artists-social-insurance-fund/) to learn more.
